programme_transition.transfer_summary: Your Sociology courses are a starting point for the wider Social Sciences & Behavioural Research field. Course links show recorded learning goals, not proof that you have mastered them. Begin with three shared, required foundations: frame a research question, judge what evidence can support and communicate what it shows. Then compare methods by the questions they can answer and the evidence they use. Choose a method or a named combined research design (a plan that uses methods together or in a stated order and explains how their findings connect). The journey then shows the domain learning, areas of specialization and roles supported by that choice, with the reason each appears. Optional items can be skipped; conditional items apply only in their stated context.
programme_transition.transferable_learning_summary: Analysing social structures and societal dynamics; using core ideas about culture and socialisation; examining human behaviour.

aggregate_count_audit.learner_display_policy: Do not display aggregate counts; use only individually resolved course/outcome evidence and its explanation.

programme_transition.domain_overview: The social sciences study people, groups and societies: how people relate, how shared arrangements such as families, schools, workplaces and governments shape everyday life, and how societies change. A research question guides what evidence (information that can help answer it) researchers gather or examine and which research methods (planned ways to gather or examine information) they use. Researchers compare evidence with possible explanations and report what it supports, what remains uncertain and why.
programme_transition.transition_policy: Show all programme themes and their outcomes together at the programme level. At the domain transition, carry only explicit, source-matched course/outcome context as prior learning; distinguish it from the additional domain foundations and optional route learning. Curriculum connections are not claims of mastery.

domain-item:d078-secondary-data.condition: Use when empirical population, behaviour or outcome data are reused to construct, calibrate or compare the model; an abstract theoretical model may not need this route.
domain-item:d078-secondary-data.rationale: Agent-based modelling has documented model-specification, empirical-grounding, evaluation and reproducibility practices; apply this item only for the stated model use case.

domain-item:d078-secondary-data.condition: Show when existing datasets, reports, archives or records are used to identify drivers or ground scenario assumptions.
domain-item:d078-secondary-data.rationale: Futures work can build an evidence base, while secondary-data learning is needed only if existing data or records are part of that evidence base.

domain-item:sampling-recruitment-and-rep.condition: Use when agents are intended to represent a real population or sampled cases; state the population, coverage and limits. Do not apply this as a requirement to abstract models without population-representation claims.
domain-item:sampling-recruitment-and-rep.rationale: Agent-based modelling has documented model-specification, empirical-grounding, evaluation and reproducibility practices; apply this item only for the stated model use case.

domain-item:sampling-recruitment-and-rep.condition: Show when the project uses a Delphi panel, expert consultation or stakeholder input and must explain whose views were included or left out.
domain-item:sampling-recruitment-and-rep.rationale: The toolkit includes panel and stakeholder methods; sampling matters only for those consultation routes and does not make a panel representative by default.

domain-item:measurement-and-operationali.condition: Use to translate social concepts and observed behaviours into explicit agent attributes, rules, parameters or measurable outputs; distinguish observed evidence from assumptions.
domain-item:measurement-and-operationali.rationale: Agent-based modelling has documented model-specification, empirical-grounding, evaluation and reproducibility practices; apply this item only for the stated model use case.

domain-item:measurement-and-operationali.condition: Show when the learner defines observable drivers, indicators or early-warning signals to compare or monitor scenarios.
domain-item:measurement-and-operationali.rationale: Driver mapping and monitoring can use defined indicators, but narrative scenario work does not always quantify its drivers.

domain-item:reliability-validity-and-unc.condition: Use to check implementation against the design, examine sensitivity to assumptions/parameters and assess whether conclusions are supported; validation is purpose-dependent and does not prove the model is true.
domain-item:reliability-validity-and-unc.rationale: Agent-based modelling has documented model-specification, empirical-grounding, evaluation and reproducibility practices; apply this item only for the stated model use case.

domain-item:reliability-validity-and-unc.condition: Show when the project evaluates evidence quality or explains uncertainty and assumptions behind its scenarios; do not treat scenarios as forecasts.
domain-item:reliability-validity-and-unc.rationale: Both toolkits frame futures as uncertain possibilities and support stress-testing assumptions; this item helps learners explain the evidence limits and uncertainty.

dispositions.condition: Show only when this scenario project uses AI-assisted survey work or digital-trace evidence; AI is not part of scenario analysis by default.
dispositions.rationale: The item is relevant only to the specified AI/survey or digital-evidence extension, not to ordinary scenario construction.

dispositions.condition: Show when the project collects, receives, analyses, stores or shares data to support its drivers, scenarios or evaluation.
dispositions.rationale: Scenario projects may use evidence and data, but this practice is relevant only when the project actually handles research data.

dispositions.condition: Show when the project consults people, uses identifiable or sensitive records, or creates a risk of harm through its evidence gathering or dissemination.
dispositions.rationale: The toolkit includes consultation methods; the ethics practice applies to the actual participants, information and risks, not to scenario writing alone.

dispositions.condition: Show when existing datasets, reports, archives or records are used to identify drivers or ground scenario assumptions.
dispositions.rationale: Futures work can build an evidence base, while secondary-data learning is needed only if existing data or records are part of that evidence base.

dispositions.condition: Show when the learner defines observable drivers, indicators or early-warning signals to compare or monitor scenarios.
dispositions.rationale: Driver mapping and monitoring can use defined indicators, but narrative scenario work does not always quantify its drivers.

dispositions.condition: Show when the learner needs others to inspect or revisit the evidence, assumptions, scenario-building steps or stress-test settings.
dispositions.rationale: A traceable record helps explain how scenarios and policy stress-tests were constructed; it is useful documentation, not a compulsory experimental preregistration.

dispositions.condition: Show when trends, disruptions, drivers or scenario assumptions are being grounded in sources that must be checked and cited.
dispositions.rationale: The foresight guidance calls for evidence gathering and evidence-informed potential disruptions; source organization supports that task.

dispositions.condition: Show when the project evaluates evidence quality or explains uncertainty and assumptions behind its scenarios; do not treat scenarios as forecasts.
dispositions.rationale: Both toolkits frame futures as uncertain possibilities and support stress-testing assumptions; this item helps learners explain the evidence limits and uncertainty.

dispositions.condition: Show when the project uses a Delphi panel, expert consultation or stakeholder input and must explain whose views were included or left out.
dispositions.rationale: The toolkit includes panel and stakeholder methods; sampling matters only for those consultation routes and does not make a panel representative by default.

dispositions.condition: This describes the field being studied and stays in domain orientation; it is not extra preparation specific to scenario analysis.
dispositions.rationale: The existing graph contract places society/social-world knowledge before methods as orientation, not inside a method route.

src:columbia-social-network-analysis.publisher: Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health
src:columbia-social-network-analysis.supports: Network analysis represents actors and their ties and can describe patterns in relationships.
src:columbia-social-network-analysis.locator: Overview of social network representations, actors, ties and network measures.
src:columbia-social-network-analysis.limits: The representation and measures answer only the defined relationship question; they do not by themselves establish why a relationship exists.

src:networkx-social-analysis-learning.title: NetworkX Guides: Facebook Network Analysis
src:networkx-social-analysis-learning.supports: Free applied tutorial showing a social-network dataset represented and analysed with NetworkX.
src:networkx-social-analysis-learning.limits: A Facebook friend-network example; not a general sampling/ethics guide and not transferable as a claim about other populations.

src:networkx-official-tutorial.title: NetworkX official tutorial
src:networkx-official-tutorial.supports: Official reference for representing graph nodes/edges, attributes and basic graph operations; appropriate as a tool learning resource after the method is chosen.
src:networkx-official-tutorial.limits: Software documentation teaches implementation, not sound social-network research design, data collection or ethical practice.

src:mixed-methods-designs.title: Fetters, Curry & Creswell: Achieving Integration in Mixed Methods Designs
src:mixed-methods-designs.supports: Exploratory sequential, explanatory sequential and convergent mixed-method designs; integration must be planned across design, methods and interpretation.
src:mixed-methods-designs.limits: Methods paper, with health-care examples; it supports design logic, not a claim that every D078 task needs mixed methods.

src:questionnaire-development-qualitativ.title: Selecting, Designing, and Developing Your Questionnaire
src:questionnaire-development-qualitativ.supports: Qualitative exploration, including focus groups, can inform questionnaire concepts and response ranges; surveys are not suitable for every question.
src:questionnaire-development-qualitativ.limits: Questionnaire-development guidance; it does not make focus groups mandatory before every survey.

src:survey-questionnaire-development.title: Developing Questionnaires for Educational Research: AMEE Guide No. 87
src:survey-questionnaire-development.supports: Interview/focus-group input, cognitive interviews and pilot testing as possible questionnaire development stages.
src:survey-questionnaire-development.limits: Education/health research guidance; transfer the method logic, not domain-specific requirements.

src:survey-mixed-methods.title: Mixed Methods and Survey Research in Family Medicine and Community Health
src:survey-mixed-methods.supports: Surveys can precede qualitative follow-up, follow qualitative exploration, or be compared with concurrent qualitative evidence in mixed-method designs.
src:survey-mixed-methods.limits: Health/community examples; does not establish that any particular social-science study needs both.

src:case-study-multiple-evidence.title: The Case Study Approach
src:case-study-multiple-evidence.supports: Case studies may combine questionnaires, interviews, focus groups and observation as multiple sources of evidence.
src:case-study-multiple-evidence.limits: Health-services examples; the evidence-source logic is general but not a universal recipe.

src:case-study-research-guide.title: Case studies: a guide for researchers, educators, and implementers
src:case-study-research-guide.supports: A bounded case can use documents, interviews, ethnographic observation, focus groups and quantitative data; source choice follows the case question.
src:case-study-research-guide.limits: Practical guide; it does not imply all sources must be collected in every case study.

src:document-elicitation-interviews.title: Participant-created documents as an elicitation tool
src:document-elicitation-interviews.supports: Documents can prompt interviews in which authors explain the meaning and context of their records.
src:document-elicitation-interviews.limits: Illustrative qualitative technique; it is conditional on suitable documents, consent and a relevant question.

src:participatory-route-area-evidence.title: D078 area/role task set and route crosswalk
src:participatory-route-area-evidence.supports: D078 task routes for participatory/action research, citizen participation, community evidence and evaluation.
src:participatory-route-area-evidence.limits: Local reviewed task-route evidence; not a universal requirement or proof that a particular method combination is appropriate.

src:ukri-research-data-policy-2026.title: UKRI Research Data Policy
src:ukri-research-data-policy-2026.supports: Research data are information collected, created, generated, observed or derived from existing sources through any research method; supports data-care preparation when a selected project handles such data.
src:ukri-research-data-policy-2026.locator: Policy statement and definition of research data
src:ukri-research-data-policy-2026.limits: A general policy, not a claim that every project must publicly share data or use the same management plan.

src:esrc-ethics-principles.title: ESRC Framework for Research Ethics: Core Principles
src:esrc-ethics-principles.supports: Ethical reflection applies across a research lifecycle; specific participant, privacy, harm and governance duties depend on the project and method.
src:esrc-ethics-principles.limits: Does not make every method ethically identical or establish a universal method prerequisite.

src:uk-data-service-qualitative-reuse.title: UK Data Service: Qualitative Data and Reuse
src:uk-data-service-qualitative-reuse.supports: Existing qualitative records such as interview transcripts, diaries, field notes and open-ended responses can be reused; qualitative and quantitative evidence can also be combined where justified.
src:uk-data-service-qualitative-reuse.locator: Qualitative data and Reusing qualitative data sections
src:uk-data-service-qualitative-reuse.limits: Reuse depends on data access, consent, context, documentation and fit to the new question.

src:uk-data-service-secondary-analysis.title: UK Data Service: New to Using Data
src:uk-data-service-secondary-analysis.supports: Secondary analysis reuses previously collected qualitative or quantitative data for a new question; social-science datasets are gathered using a range of methods.
src:uk-data-service-secondary-analysis.locator: Secondary analysis and types of social-science data sections
src:uk-data-service-secondary-analysis.limits: A new question still requires checking data provenance, access permissions, population/period coverage, measures and original collection context.

src:abm-empirical-social-research.title: Agent-Based Models in Empirical Social Research
src:abm-empirical-social-research.supports: Agent-based models represent actors following rules and require justified construction, evaluation and careful interpretation when compared with empirical evidence.
src:abm-empirical-social-research.locator: Abstract and sections on model construction, empirical grounding, evaluation and sensitivity analysis.
src:abm-empirical-social-research.limits: Fit to observed data and sensitivity checks do not make every model a universal prediction.

src:comses-odd-standards.title: CoMSES Net: Agent-Based Model Documentation Standards
src:comses-odd-standards.supports: The ODD protocol documents an agent-based model's overview, design concepts and implementation details to make models understandable and reusable.
src:comses-odd-standards.locator: Standards > Documentation Standards > The ODD Protocol
src:comses-odd-standards.limits: Documentation guidance, not a guarantee that a model is valid or empirically representative.

src:par-methods-nature-2023.title: Participatory Action Research
src:par-methods-nature-2023.supports: Participatory action research shares leadership with people experiencing an issue and uses collaborative inquiry, evidence generation, analysis and action.
src:par-methods-nature-2023.locator: Primer abstract and sections describing PAR project design building blocks
src:par-methods-nature-2023.limits: Supports the participatory framework and its design logic; does not establish that every component-method set is suitable for every question or area.

src:cdc-field-epi-qualitative-2024.title: Collecting and Analyzing Qualitative Data
src:cdc-field-epi-qualitative-2024.supports: Describes interviews, focus-group discussions and observation as qualitative evidence methods, their uses and limitations.
src:cdc-field-epi-qualitative-2024.locator: Chapter sections on interviews, focus groups, observation and recruitment
src:cdc-field-epi-qualitative-2024.limits: Field-epidemiology guidance; supports method identity and use, not a universal D078 area or role assignment.

src:cdc-evaluation-method-selection-2024.title: Step 4 – Gather Credible Evidence
src:cdc-evaluation-method-selection-2024.supports: Describes surveys, interviews, observation, focus groups and purposeful integration of qualitative and quantitative evidence, with selection based on the evaluation question and community context.
src:cdc-evaluation-method-selection-2024.locator: Common Data Collection Methods and mixed-methods guidance
src:cdc-evaluation-method-selection-2024.limits: Evaluation guidance; supports method-selection logic, not a claim that every combination is required or interchangeable.

src:unisa-community-engaged-research-201.title: Policy on Research Ethics: Guidelines for Community-Engaged Research
src:unisa-community-engaged-research-201.supports: Treats participatory action research as an orientation to research rather than a data-collection technique; states that community-engaged work may use quantitative, qualitative or combined data-gathering methods shaped by context.
src:unisa-community-engaged-research-201.limits: Institutional ethics policy; supports the distinction between participatory orientation and evidence methods, not D078-specific area or role assignments.

src:zotero-official-quick-start.title: Zotero official quick-start guide
src:zotero-official-quick-start.supports: Reference management: collecting, organizing and citing sources including books, reports, webpages, letters and manuscripts.
src:zotero-official-quick-start.limits: Does not judge evidence quality or interpret source content.

src:tropy-official-documentation.title: Tropy official documentation
src:tropy-official-documentation.supports: Organizing and describing photographs of research materials with metadata, tags and notes.
src:tropy-official-documentation.limits: Explicitly not a citation manager or qualitative-analysis system.

src:taguette-getting-started.title: Taguette official getting-started guide
src:taguette-getting-started.supports: Document upload, code/tag creation, annotation and retrieval of coded passages.
src:taguette-getting-started.limits: Does not generate a valid interpretation or decide what codes mean.

src:taguette-official-app.title: Taguette official project page
src:taguette-official-app.supports: Open-source web-based document tagging for qualitative data analysis.
src:taguette-official-app.limits: Product description is not a substitute for qualitative-method instruction.

src:nvivo-official-desktop.title: Lumivero NVivo Desktop official product documentation
src:nvivo-official-desktop.supports: Organizing, coding, querying and comparing interviews, documents, surveys and multimedia, including mixed-methods workflows.
src:nvivo-official-desktop.limits: Vendor capability statement; commercial licensing and data governance must be checked.

src:r-time-series-manual.title: R stats package: time-series objects
src:r-time-series-manual.supports: Representing numeric observations indexed by time and frequency.
src:r-time-series-manual.limits: Documentation for data representation; does not establish a suitable economic model or inference.

src:stata-time-series.title: Stata official time-series features
src:stata-time-series.supports: Time-series analysis, models, diagnostics and forecasting features.
src:stata-time-series.limits: Product documentation; software access, assumptions and data quality remain separate considerations.

src:eviews-time-series-regression.title: EViews official help: time-series regression
src:eviews-time-series-regression.supports: ARMA, ARIMA and ARFIMA specifications and diagnostics for time-series data.
src:eviews-time-series-regression.limits: Commercial tool; software help does not determine whether the model fits the research question or data.

external:stata-why-use-stata-2026.title: Why use Stata
external:stata-why-use-stata-2026.locator: Data manipulation and analysis; panel, multilevel, survey, time-series data; reproducible workflows.
external:stata-why-use-stata-2026.supports: Stata's documented capabilities for structured-data and quantitative-analysis workflows.
external:stata-why-use-stata-2026.scope_limit: Product documentation supports software-function claims only; it does not make Stata necessary for every learner or research design.

external:stata-survey-methods-2026.title: Survey methods
external:stata-survey-methods-2026.locator: Survey-design adjustment, descriptive statistics, regression, panel-data, multilevel and item-response workflows.
external:stata-survey-methods-2026.supports: A bounded relationship between Stata and quantitative survey/data-analysis tasks when the sampling design and analysis justify it.
external:stata-survey-methods-2026.scope_limit: The learner must understand the design, weights, assumptions and interpretation; software output is not a validity guarantee.

external:stata-video-tutorials-2026.title: Video tutorials
external:stata-video-tutorials-2026.locator: Official task-based videos include descriptive statistics, regression, time series, panel data, tests and reporting.
external:stata-video-tutorials-2026.supports: A direct, free instructional link for learning specific Stata tasks.
external:stata-video-tutorials-2026.scope_limit: Tutorial availability does not establish that learners need licensed Stata software or must choose it over another tool.

external:nuc-social-sciences-ccmas-2023.title: Social Sciences CCMAS 2023
external:nuc-social-sciences-ccmas-2023.locator: Sociology SSC 401 Research Method II: apply appropriate statistics in data analysis; curriculum context only.
external:nuc-social-sciences-ccmas-2023.supports: Nigerian social-science curriculum context for quantitative analysis.
external:nuc-social-sciences-ccmas-2023.scope_limit: Does not prescribe Stata or establish it as a programme requirement.

external:r-project-about-2026.title: What is R?
external:r-project-about-2026.locator: Official overview: statistical computing, graphics, modelling, tests, time-series analysis and extensibility.
external:r-project-about-2026.scope_limit: Official project information does not make R necessary for a particular method, programme or role.

external:r-project-manuals-2026.title: R Manuals
external:r-project-manuals-2026.locator: Official manuals for R installation, language, data import/export, administration and extensions.
external:r-project-manuals-2026.supports: A direct official learning/reference resource for working with R.
external:r-project-manuals-2026.scope_limit: Manuals do not replace statistical reasoning or task-specific method training.

external:taguette-about-2026.title: About TAGUETTE
external:taguette-about-2026.locator: Import research documents, highlight text and apply learner-defined tags/codes; export project materials.
external:taguette-about-2026.scope_limit: It assists organizing/coding; it does not interpret evidence or determine a valid coding scheme.

external:taguette-getting-started-2026.title: Getting started with TAGUETTE
external:taguette-getting-started-2026.locator: Create a project, import a document, highlight text and apply tags; supported formats and export workflow.
external:taguette-getting-started-2026.supports: Direct practical learning resource for the tool.
external:taguette-getting-started-2026.scope_limit: Tool instructions do not replace research-method training or ethical review.

external:nvivo-desktop-2026.title: NVivo Desktop
external:nvivo-desktop-2026.locator: Researcher-led qualitative and mixed-methods software for coding, querying, comparing, visualizing and interpreting material.
external:nvivo-desktop-2026.supports: Software identity and supported qualitative workflow scope.
external:nvivo-desktop-2026.scope_limit: Commercial product; software capability does not make NVivo necessary or replace interpretation.

external:nvivo-getting-started-2026.title: Getting started basics
external:nvivo-getting-started-2026.locator: Beginner tutorials for importing data, coding, note-taking, queries and visualizations.
external:nvivo-getting-started-2026.supports: Direct instructional resource for common NVivo tasks.
external:nvivo-getting-started-2026.scope_limit: Current product/version access and licence may vary.

external:gephi-desktop-2026.title: Gephi Desktop
external:gephi-desktop-2026.locator: Official description of network exploration and visualization software, graph formats and data import.
external:gephi-desktop-2026.supports: Network-data visualization software identity and function.
external:gephi-desktop-2026.scope_limit: Visualization does not establish that a network model is appropriate or that a visual pattern proves a social claim.

external:gephi-quickstart-2026.title: Gephi Quickstart
external:gephi-quickstart-2026.locator: Import a source/target edge table or network file, inspect import, examine nodes/edges and explore a graph.
external:gephi-quickstart-2026.supports: Direct practical learning resource for network visualization.
external:gephi-quickstart-2026.scope_limit: A quickstart is not a complete course in network research design or inference.

external:ibm-spss-regression-2026.title: Linear Regression in SPSS Statistics
external:ibm-spss-regression-2026.locator: Procedure steps, numeric outcome/predictor fields, regression output, assumptions and weighted least squares options.
external:ibm-spss-regression-2026.scope_limit: Commercial software; a menu or command does not select an appropriate model or establish causal validity.

external:ibm-spss-regression-reference-2.title: REGRESSION command
external:ibm-spss-regression-reference-2.locator: Official command reference for regression equations, statistics, plots and diagnostics.
external:ibm-spss-regression-reference-2.supports: A second official reference for the tool's regression workflow.
external:ibm-spss-regression-reference-2.scope_limit: The reference documents commands, not a universal requirement to use SPSS.

external:uk-go-science-futures-toolkit.title: Government Office for Science Futures Toolkit
external:uk-go-science-futures-toolkit.supports: Evidence gathering, driver mapping, scenarios and policy stress-testing for exploring uncertainty; scenarios are possibilities, not predictions.
external:uk-go-science-futures-toolkit.limits: A policy foresight toolkit, not a universal research-method requirement or proof that every scenario project uses data, participants, or quantitative indicators.

external:oecd-foresight-toolkit-2025.title: OECD Strategic Foresight Toolkit for Resilient Public Policy
external:oecd-foresight-toolkit-2025.supports: A five-step policy foresight process for challenging assumptions, creating scenarios, stress-testing strategies and developing actions.
external:oecd-foresight-toolkit-2025.limits: Policy-foresight guidance; it does not make scenarios predictions or require every optional research practice.

external:aapor-responsible-ai-survey-202.title: AAPOR Task Force on Responsible AI Integration in Survey Research
external:aapor-responsible-ai-survey-202.supports: Data quality, transparency, human oversight, ethics and disclosure when AI is used in survey research.
external:aapor-responsible-ai-survey-202.limits: Survey-specific. Use only when the scenario project includes an AI-assisted survey or survey evidence; do not generalize it to all scenario work.

src:d078-computational-social-science-re.title: Edelmann et al., Computational Social Science and Sociology, Annual Review of Sociology (2020)
src:d078-computational-social-science-re.supports: Interdisciplinary definition of computational social science, use of computational methods with digital sources, and the importance of developing or applying social-science theory.
src:d078-computational-social-science-re.limits: A review's definition and disciplinary scope; it does not establish that all social-science research is computational or that large data are automatically valid.

src:d078-digital-trace-data-2025.title: Best practices for studies using digital data donation
src:d078-digital-trace-data-2025.supports: Digital trace data are information created through digital interactions; examples include social-media use, email and transactions.
src:d078-digital-trace-data-2025.locator: Introduction: definition and examples of digital trace data.
src:d078-digital-trace-data-2025.limits: The examples do not establish that every trace is accessible, representative, or ethically reusable.

src:d078-esrc-internet-mediated-research.title: Internet-mediated research ethics guidance
src:d078-esrc-internet-mediated-research.publisher: UK Research and Innovation, Economic and Social Research Council
src:d078-esrc-internet-mediated-research.supports: Research using online material still requires attention to privacy, consent, identifiability, platform rules and appropriate ethics review.
src:d078-esrc-internet-mediated-research.locator: Guidance sections on online material, privacy, consent, identifiability, platform rules and ethics review.
src:d078-esrc-internet-mediated-research.limits: UK guidance; apply the relevant institutional process and laws for the learner's setting.

src:d078-tool-limesurvey.title: LimeSurvey official manual: surveys and responses
src:d078-tool-limesurvey.supports: Creating and managing surveys, questions and response records.
src:d078-tool-limesurvey.limits: Software documentation verifies functions, not questionnaire validity, sample quality or research ethics.

src:d078-tool-nvivo.title: Lumivero NVivo documentation: coding qualitative material
src:d078-tool-nvivo.supports: Coding document or transcript passages and organizing references to themes, people or entities.
src:d078-tool-nvivo.limits: Software documentation verifies product functions, not the validity of a coding scheme or interpretation.

src:d078-tool-python.title: Python official tutorial
src:d078-tool-python.supports: Python is a programming language suitable for scripts and application development; the tutorial expects basic programming knowledge.
src:d078-tool-python.limits: The tutorial is not a social-science research-method guide and assumes prior programming knowledge.

src:d078-tool-r.title: The R Project: What is R?
src:d078-tool-r.supports: R is a language and environment for statistical computing and graphics with data-handling, analysis and plotting facilities.
src:d078-tool-r.limits: Official product description; method choice and research interpretation remain the learner's responsibility.

src:d078-tool-spss.title: IBM SPSS Statistics: t-test and chi-square procedures
src:d078-tool-spss.supports: SPSS procedures for comparing sample means and calculating chi-square statistics for counts in categories.
src:d078-tool-spss.limits: Software procedures have data and assumption requirements; product documentation does not make the selected method suitable for every question.

src:d078-tool-stata.title: Stata official feature guides: panel and time-series analysis
src:d078-tool-stata.supports: Stata functions for analyzing repeated panel records, group relationships and outcomes over time.
src:d078-tool-stata.limits: Commercial software documentation; included features do not establish that every procedure or route is required.

src:d078-tool-taguette.title: Taguette official site and documentation
src:d078-tool-taguette.supports: Open-source web-based tool for qualitative document tagging, annotation and retrieval.
src:d078-tool-taguette.limits: Tool description verifies document-tagging functions, not the quality of an interpretation or the generalizability of findings.

src:annual-review-css-2020.title: Edelmann et al., Computational Social Science and Sociology
src:annual-review-css-2020.supports: Computational social science combines social science with computing and engineering methods, applies computational methods to digital sources, and connects analysis with theories of human behaviour.
src:annual-review-css-2020.locator: Abstract and opening definition: computational methods applied to social-media, administrative and historical-archive data; conclusion calls for attention to sociological theory.
src:annual-review-css-2020.limits: Review definition and examples; it does not establish that all social-science work is computational or that digital data are automatically valid.

src:edinburgh-css-course.title: Understanding Society with Big Data: Computational Social Science
src:edinburgh-css-course.publisher: University of Edinburgh, Open Course Materials
src:edinburgh-css-course.supports: The course sequence includes forming social research questions, collecting data, choosing methods, text and network analysis, bias, ethics, and explaining findings and limitations.
src:edinburgh-css-course.locator: Learning Outcomes and Course Outline: question formulation; data and method choice; descriptive analysis of textual/network data; ethical challenges, bias, findings and limitations.
src:edinburgh-css-course.limits: A course outline illustrates a teaching sequence and examples; it is not a universal curriculum or a claim that every route needs every technique.

src:d078-unesco-iscoped-social-sciences.title: International Standard Classification of Education: Fields of Education and Training 2013 — Detailed Field Descriptions
src:d078-unesco-iscoped-social-sciences.supports: The classification distinguishes social and behavioural science fields including economics, political science, psychology, sociology and social geography, and describes their boundaries.
src:d078-unesco-iscoped-social-sciences.locator: Field 03 and detailed fields 031 and 0311–0314; definitions and inclusions/exclusions for social and behavioural sciences.
src:d078-unesco-iscoped-social-sciences.limits: A field-of-education classification, not a complete account of each discipline's methods, current practice or local curriculum.

src:d078-core-econ-doing-economics-2026.title: Doing Economics
src:d078-core-econ-doing-economics-2026.supports: Applied economics learning connects a defined economic question with data handling, statistical procedures, and transparent use of software; examples include tax and inequality analysis.
src:d078-core-econ-doing-economics-2026.locator: Project overview and example projects: 12 data-based projects, step-by-step use of Excel, Google Sheets, R and Python; project 3 measures sugar-tax effects using differences-in-differences; project 5 examines inequality with Gini coefficients and Lorenz curves.
src:d078-core-econ-doing-economics-2026.limits: An open teaching resource that illustrates some data-based economics projects; it is not a complete economics curriculum or a statement that every learner must use each listed tool.

src:d078-un-population-demodata-2026.title: DemoData
src:d078-un-population-demodata-2026.publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
src:d078-un-population-demodata-2026.supports: Population analysis draws on defined information about age, sex, births, deaths and migration assembled from sources such as censuses, registers and surveys; population estimates and projections depend on their sources and methods.
src:d078-un-population-demodata-2026.locator: About DemoData and data coverage: indicators, source types, compiled empirical data and tabulations used by the UN Population Division for estimates and projections.
src:d078-un-population-demodata-2026.limits: An international data resource; definitions, dates, geographic coverage and local statistical systems must be checked before using a series for a particular place.

src:d078-worldbank-rural-accessibility-m.title: Rural Accessibility Mapping
src:d078-worldbank-rural-accessibility-m.supports: Location-based analysis can combine population, roads and service locations to estimate how many people can reach a service within a stated travel time; the estimate depends on inputs and definitions.
src:d078-worldbank-rural-accessibility-m.locator: Project description: required geospatial inputs and accessibility indicators based on population share able to reach a nearby point of service within a selected time.
src:d078-worldbank-rural-accessibility-m.limits: A specific rural-accessibility example, not a universal measure of access or a substitute for local validation of roads, service locations and travel conditions.

src:d078-oecd-regulatory-impact-policy.title: Recommendation of the Council on Regulatory Policy and Governance
src:d078-oecd-regulatory-impact-policy.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
src:d078-oecd-regulatory-impact-policy.supports: Public decisions can be examined by defining a problem, checking evidence for action, comparing policy instruments and considering expected benefits, costs, distribution and implementation needs.
src:d078-oecd-regulatory-impact-policy.locator: Sections on defining the problem and assessing whether government action is justified; discussion of alternative mechanisms, benefits and costs, distribution, and administrative requirements.
src:d078-oecd-regulatory-impact-policy.limits: International recommendation rather than a Nigerian statute; its analysis prompts do not replace the relevant country's laws or decision process.

src:d078-magenta-book-2026.title: Magenta Book: Central Government Guidance on Evaluation
src:d078-magenta-book-2026.publisher: HM Treasury and UK Government Social Research
src:d078-magenta-book-2026.supports: Evaluation asks whether an intervention was delivered as intended, what changed, for whom and why; process, impact and value-for-money questions need suitable evidence and methods.
src:d078-magenta-book-2026.locator: Chapters 1.8 and 1.9: process, impact and value-for-money evaluation; theory of change, testing explanations, combining approaches and limits to attribution or generalisation.
src:d078-magenta-book-2026.limits: UK central-government guidance; examples and institutional requirements are jurisdiction-specific and must not be presented as binding Nigerian procedure.

src:d078-openstax-psychology-research-2e.title: Approaches to Research, Psychology 2e
src:d078-openstax-psychology-research-2e.supports: Research questions determine whether observation, surveys, interviews or experiments are appropriate, and each approach has different strengths and limits.
src:d078-openstax-psychology-research-2e.locator: Section 2.2: description of observational, survey, interview and experimental approaches and their differing strengths and limits.
src:d078-openstax-psychology-research-2e.limits: An introductory psychology textbook example; this D078 area covers social-science questions and does not teach clinical assessment or treatment.

src:d078-openstax-social-influence-2e.title: Conformity, Compliance, and Obedience, Psychology 2e
src:d078-openstax-social-influence-2e.supports: Social settings and group processes can influence people's thoughts, feelings and actions; study examples also require attention to how a behavior was measured and the limits of a particular study.
src:d078-openstax-social-influence-2e.locator: Section 12.4 opening and sections on conformity, social influence and group processes.
src:d078-openstax-social-influence-2e.limits: Illustrative introductory material; a classic study does not establish a universal rule about all people or settings.

src:d078-openstax-sociology-research-3e.title: Sociological Research, Introduction to Sociology 3e
src:d078-openstax-sociology-research-3e.supports: Sociological research begins with a question and a study plan; surveys, observation, interviews, experiments and existing sources answer different kinds of questions and carry different limits.
src:d078-openstax-sociology-research-3e.locator: Section 2.2: research design and examples of primary data collection and secondary analysis; method choice depends on the question and context.
src:d078-openstax-sociology-research-3e.limits: An introductory textbook, not a substitute for local curriculum or research ethics requirements.

src:d078-openstax-anthropology-culture.title: Culture, Introduction to Anthropology
src:d078-openstax-anthropology-culture.supports: Anthropology studies how people meet needs and organize life in different social and environmental settings; culture is a central concept and is learned, created and changed.
src:d078-openstax-anthropology-culture.locator: Chapter 3 introduction: everyday needs, social circumstances, differing practices and the study of culture and change.
src:d078-openstax-anthropology-culture.limits: An introductory cultural-anthropology account; it is an example of disciplinary scope, not a claim that all anthropology uses one method.

src:d078-aaa-anthropological-ethics.title: Anthropological Ethics
src:d078-aaa-anthropological-ethics.supports: Anthropological research should avoid harm, be open about the work, obtain informed consent and necessary permissions, consider affected parties, make results accessible and protect records.
src:d078-aaa-anthropological-ethics.locator: Principles of Professional Responsibility listed on the association page.
src:d078-aaa-anthropological-ethics.limits: Professional ethical guidance, not a replacement for local law, institutional review or community-specific obligations.

src:d078-aapor-survey-best-practices.title: Best Practices for Survey Research
src:d078-aapor-survey-best-practices.publisher: American Association for Public Opinion Research
src:d078-aapor-survey-best-practices.supports: Survey suitability, question and sample planning, recruitment, survey modes, disclosure and limitations of probability and non-probability samples.
src:d078-aapor-survey-best-practices.locator: Best Practices sections on survey planning, sampling, data collection and transparent reporting.
src:d078-aapor-survey-best-practices.limits: Professional guidance, not a guarantee that a particular survey is valid or representative.

src:d078-aapor-transparency-initiative.title: Transparency Initiative
src:d078-aapor-transparency-initiative.publisher: American Association for Public Opinion Research
src:d078-aapor-transparency-initiative.supports: Disclosure of sample selection, recruitment, survey mode, question wording, weighting and content-analysis procedures.
src:d078-aapor-transparency-initiative.locator: Transparency Initiative required disclosure items for sampling, recruitment, measurement, analysis and reporting.
src:d078-aapor-transparency-initiative.limits: A transparency standard; disclosure by itself does not establish that a study is sound.

src:d078-cosmin-measurement-properties.title: Explanation and Elaboration for the COSMIN Reporting Guideline 2.0
src:d078-cosmin-measurement-properties.supports: Consensus terminology for constructs and the measurement properties used to assess instruments, including reliability and validity.
src:d078-cosmin-measurement-properties.locator: Terminology and abbreviations; measurement-property definitions and the distinction between the construct being measured and instrument quality.
src:d078-cosmin-measurement-properties.limits: Developed for outcome-measurement instruments, especially patient-reported measures; use as a measurement-method source, not as a claim that all D078 scales are clinical instruments.

src:d078-aera-apa-ncme-testing-standards.title: Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing
src:d078-aera-apa-ncme-testing-standards.publisher: American Educational Research Association, American Psychological Association and National Council on Measurement in Education
src:d078-aera-apa-ncme-testing-standards.supports: Professional standards for test development, score interpretation, validity, reliability and fairness.
src:d078-aera-apa-ncme-testing-standards.locator: Overview of the joint Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing and their scope.
src:d078-aera-apa-ncme-testing-standards.limits: The standards guide tests and score use; they do not certify any particular D078 measure or scale.

src:d078-statsmodels-arima.title: ARIMA models
src:d078-statsmodels-arima.supports: The ARIMA interface includes autoregressive, moving-average, ARMA, ARIMA and seasonal variants and permits regression with ARIMA-type errors.
src:d078-statsmodels-arima.locator: Class description and supported AR, MA, ARMA, ARIMA and seasonal model variants.
src:d078-statsmodels-arima.limits: Software documentation identifies model forms; it does not establish that a model is appropriate for a particular series or research question.

src:d078-statsmodels-mixedlm.title: Linear Mixed Effects Models
src:d078-statsmodels-mixedlm.supports: The statsmodels reference documents linear mixed-effects models and variance components used to represent grouped or multilevel data.
src:d078-statsmodels-mixedlm.locator: Linear Mixed Effects Models guide and MixedLM/variance-component API descriptions.
src:d078-statsmodels-mixedlm.limits: Software documentation describes model implementations; it does not determine whether a multilevel model is appropriate for a particular research question or dataset.

src:d078-worldbank-dime-longitudinal-pan.title: Chapter 3: Establishing a Measurement Framework
src:d078-worldbank-dime-longitudinal-pan.publisher: World Bank, Development Impact Evaluation (DIME) Analytics Data Handbook
src:d078-worldbank-dime-longitudinal-pan.supports: The handbook distinguishes longitudinal repeated observations from repeated cross-sections and panel data, where the same units are observed over time.
src:d078-worldbank-dime-longitudinal-pan.locator: Discussion of longitudinal observations, repeated cross-sections and panel data.
src:d078-worldbank-dime-longitudinal-pan.limits: The handbook is oriented to development-impact evaluation; this data-structure distinction does not establish a causal design by itself.

src:d078-worldbank-dime-panel-data-const.title: Chapter 6: Constructing and Analyzing Research Data
src:d078-worldbank-dime-panel-data-const.publisher: World Bank, Development Impact Evaluation (DIME) Analytics Data Handbook
src:d078-worldbank-dime-panel-data-const.supports: The handbook describes appending baseline and endline records to create panel data and recommends documenting unmatched records and sample differences.
src:d078-worldbank-dime-panel-data-const.locator: Panel-data construction and record-matching discussion in the analysis chapter.
src:d078-worldbank-dime-panel-data-const.limits: The handbook is oriented to development-impact evaluation; the construction steps do not establish that any particular panel analysis is appropriate.

src:d078-sage-dictionary-discourse-analy.title: Discourse Analysis
src:d078-sage-dictionary-discourse-analy.publisher: SAGE Publications, The SAGE Dictionary of Social Research Methods
src:d078-sage-dictionary-discourse-analy.supports: Discourse analysis is a family of qualitative approaches that examines texts, conversations and documents in context, including connections among language, communication, knowledge, power and social practices.
src:d078-sage-dictionary-discourse-analy.locator: Publisher chapter record: definition and distinctive features.
src:d078-sage-dictionary-discourse-analy.limits: The publisher record presents a broad definition of a heterogeneous family; particular discourse-analytic traditions use different theories and procedures, and full chapter access may require a subscription.

src:d078-nist-machine-learning-glossary.title: Machine Learning
src:d078-nist-machine-learning-glossary.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
src:d078-nist-machine-learning-glossary.supports: A standards glossary description of computer systems that adapt from data, interpreted in context with the cited NIST source.
src:d078-nist-machine-learning-glossary.locator: NIST CSRC glossary entry for machine learning and its linked source publications.
src:d078-nist-machine-learning-glossary.limits: The glossary definition is broad; it is not a claim that every computational social-science method is machine learning.

src:d078-ucla-conversation-analysis.title: Conversation Analysis
src:d078-ucla-conversation-analysis.publisher: University of California, Los Angeles, Department of Sociology
src:d078-ucla-conversation-analysis.supports: Conversation analysis studies interaction closely as turns and actions unfold, using recorded interaction and participants' responses as evidence for interpretation.
src:d078-ucla-conversation-analysis.locator: Overview of the approach, its sequential questions and its use of audio/video recordings, transcripts and annotation.
src:d078-ucla-conversation-analysis.limits: A university working-group overview of one methodological tradition; it does not represent every discourse-analytic approach.

src:d078-asa-pvalue-statement.title: ASA Statement on Statistical Significance and P-Values
src:d078-asa-pvalue-statement.supports: The meaning and limits of p-values and statistical-significance thresholds, including why they do not measure effect size or whether a hypothesis is true.
src:d078-asa-pvalue-statement.locator: The six principles in the ASA statement.
src:d078-asa-pvalue-statement.limits: A statement about statistical interpretation; it does not replace the design-specific assumptions of an analysis.

ISA_DIGITAL_SOCIOLOGY.title: WG10 Digital Sociology
ISA_DIGITAL_SOCIOLOGY.supports: The ISA working group identifies research at the intersection of digital technologies and society, including theoretical, empirical, methodological and socioethical work.
ISA_DIGITAL_SOCIOLOGY.limits: This establishes a recognized research focus, not a requirement that all social research use computational methods.

UNESCO_ISCED_FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.title: International Standard Classification of Education: Fields of Education and Training 2013 — Detailed Field Descriptions
UNESCO_ISCED_FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.supports: The detailed classification describes social and behavioural science fields and gives inclusion and exclusion examples that distinguish adjacent fields.
UNESCO_ISCED_FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.locator: Detailed descriptions for broad field 03 and narrow field 031, including economics, political science, psychology, sociology and cultural studies.
UNESCO_ISCED_FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS.limits: An education-field classification used to describe programme content; it is not a complete map of contemporary research areas or work practice.

UNESCO_ISCED_SOCIAL_SCIENCES.title: International Standard Classification of Education: Fields of Education and Training 2013 — Detailed Field Descriptions
UNESCO_ISCED_SOCIAL_SCIENCES.supports: The classification sets out the social and behavioural science field, its component subjects and boundaries with adjacent fields.
UNESCO_ISCED_SOCIAL_SCIENCES.locator: Field 03 and detailed field 031, including codes 0311–0314 and related exclusions.
UNESCO_ISCED_SOCIAL_SCIENCES.limits: An international education classification, not a complete account of every social-science discipline or current professional practice.

UNESCO_SOCIAL_SCIENCE_DEFINITION.title: Social Sciences (for R&D Data)
UNESCO_SOCIAL_SCIENCE_DEFINITION.publisher: UNESCO Institute for Statistics, UIS Data Browser Glossary
UNESCO_SOCIAL_SCIENCE_DEFINITION.supports: Defines the social-science grouping used in research-and-development statistics and lists fields such as psychology, economics, sociology, law, political science, geography and media and communications.
UNESCO_SOCIAL_SCIENCE_DEFINITION.locator: UIS Data Browser glossary entry 2462; definition and its Frascati Manual source.
UNESCO_SOCIAL_SCIENCE_DEFINITION.limits: A statistical classification definition for R&D reporting, not a full disciplinary description or a learning-path specification.

src:d078-jasp-student-guide-2025.title: Statistical Analysis in JASP: A Guide for Students (2025)
src:d078-jasp-student-guide-2025.supports: The official guide documents JASP's menu-based workflow and examples for t-tests, ANOVA, regression, contingency tables, and frequentist and Bayesian analyses.
src:d078-jasp-student-guide-2025.locator: Analysis menu and corresponding student-guide chapters; supports documented software capabilities, not a recommendation that JASP fits every study.
src:d078-jasp-student-guide-2025.limits: A software guide, not independent evidence that an analysis is appropriate for a particular research question or dataset.

src:d078-openstax-sociology-scope-3e.title: What Is Sociology? Introduction to Sociology 3e
src:d078-openstax-sociology-scope-3e.supports: Sociology studies groups and group interactions, societies and social interactions from close relationships to large social settings.
src:d078-openstax-sociology-scope-3e.locator: Section 1.1 opening definition and discussion of society, social institutions and individual/group settings.
src:d078-openstax-sociology-scope-3e.limits: An introductory textbook account; examples explain core scope but do not cover every sociological tradition or local curriculum.

src:d078-esrc-research-consent.title: Consent: Research Ethics Guidance
src:d078-esrc-research-consent.publisher: UK Research and Innovation, Economic and Social Research Council
src:d078-esrc-research-consent.supports: Informed consent requires enough accessible information for a voluntary decision; it includes what participation and data use involve, possible withdrawal, and limits to confidentiality where relevant.
src:d078-esrc-research-consent.locator: Sections 'What is freely given informed consent?', 'Giving information to participants', 'Consent', and voluntary participation/withdrawal guidance.
src:d078-esrc-research-consent.limits: UKRI/ESRC guidance; the applicable institution, local ethics process and law govern each study. Consent can require a justified alternative in some designs.

src:d078-ons-administrative-data-glossar.title: Administrative Data Census Project Glossary
src:d078-ons-administrative-data-glossar.supports: Administrative data are information people have already provided to government while accessing public services; related records are made for service and administrative purposes.
src:d078-ons-administrative-data-glossar.locator: Administrative data entry and examples of information supplied while accessing public services.
src:d078-ons-administrative-data-glossar.limits: The examples and data systems are UK-specific; they support the general distinction between service records and research-collected information, not a claim about every country's records.

src:d078-ons-what-are-data.title: What Are Data?
src:d078-ons-what-are-data.supports: Data are collected facts and figures that can appear as numbers, words or images; they require interpretation before they become useful information.
src:d078-ons-what-are-data.locator: Opening definition, quantitative and qualitative examples, and section 'How do we use data to create statistics?'.
src:d078-ons-what-are-data.limits: An introductory statistics-agency explanation, not a full information-science definition; its examples reflect UK official statistics.

integration_contract.selection_rule: required participatory frame plus one or more explicitly selected component methods
integration_contract.framework_role: Participatory action research is the shared governance and inquiry orientation; the selected components are evidence-gathering methods used within that orientation.
integration_contract.area_rule: intersection of method_area_route.area_id for every active method
integration_contract.role_rule: intersection of method_area_role_route.role_id within each eligible area for every active method
integration_contract.content_rule: Expose only contribution records attached to the selected methods' source route IDs; preserve item/tool/role-item ownership and requirement lanes.
integration_contract.no_inference_rule: A missing method-area or method-area-role source route excludes that branch. Do not substitute another area's or method's route.
integration_contract.external_evidence_scope: External sources support the participatory orientation, method-choice logic and cautions; they do not independently assert each D078 area/role pairing or certify every selected method set.
integration_contract.local_route_evidence_scope: Each variant preserves the exact reviewed method-area and method-area-role route node IDs used to derive its intersections.
integration_contract.student_explanation: Choose one evidence method or combine several when they fit your research question and community agreement. The app keeps an area or role only when the graph supports every method you selected there.
integration_contract.limits: The selectable sets are route configurations, not 15 universally recommended or named research designs. Method suitability, participation, power, consent, access and safety remain question- and community-specific.

method_combination_selection_contract.multi_selection_policy: Never project the union of independently selected methods. Resolve the complete selected set to exact named design(s); if several designs match, require a design choice. Incomplete larger designs and unsupported sets have no combined downstream.
method_combination_selection_contract.single_selection_policy: One selected method projects only its own route; no combined design is required or implied.
method_combination_selection_contract.dominance_policy: Method contribution may be asymmetric. Keep each component's contribution explicit; do not require equal weighting or use dominance to expand into areas/roles without route evidence.

area_task_family_selection_contract.purpose: Let the learner focus on one or more kinds of work in the selected area and see only the evidence-linked learning and role-task context for those focuses.
area_task_family_selection_contract.selectable_family_source: task_family_ids in the exact selected method_area_route or combination_area_route, intersected with family nodes marked approved_for_optional_area_task_focus
area_task_family_selection_contract.maximum_selections: all eligible families in the exact route
area_task_family_selection_contract.no_family_selected_behavior: Keep the general route for the selected area available; do not block or hide the area.
area_task_family_selection_contract.family_to_area_item_behavior: Use resolved task_has_area_learning_item edges for the selected family IDs; retain area-item ownership, condition and requirement lane; deduplicate the same canonical item reached from multiple selected families and explain each supporting family.
area_task_family_selection_contract.domain_item_carry_forward_behavior: Use domain_item_supports_area_task edges to show which already-selected domain items support the selected focus. Keep those items domain-owned and selected only once. An unselected upstream item may be offered as an optional add, but is not silently added or made a blocker.
area_task_family_selection_contract.role_behavior: Show a role-task context only through a resolved area_task_family_supports_role_task edge and the existing role route for the selected area/design. A role may connect to multiple selected families; deduplicate the role card and retain each task-context explanation.
area_task_family_selection_contract.role_item_behavior: Role-owned items remain available after opening the role. Do not claim a role item is specific to a selected family unless a separate reviewed role-task-to-role-item edge exists.
area_task_family_selection_contract.combined_design_behavior: Use task_family_ids and method_contributions from the exact named design route; do not union standalone-method routes by default.
area_task_family_selection_contract.item_blocking_policy: Task-family selection and all family-context edges are non-blocking. Item-level requirement lanes and approved dependency edges remain authoritative.
area_task_family_selection_contract.route_order_policy: Task families are parallel work-context choices, not a sequence. Sequence items only by an explicit reviewed sequence edge.

D078:computational-digital-social-scienc.reason: A computational question-framing item already exists and can be reused once before work-family choices.

D078:economics-applied-analysis.reason: Economic concepts and indicators add area subject knowledge beyond generic research-question design.

D078:human-geography-population.reason: Place, spatial representation and scale orient the area; population-specific measures remain route/task-specific.

D078:politics-governance-public-policy.reason: Institutions, public authority and policy process are shared subject context across the area.

D078:psychology-social-behaviour.reason: Behavioural concepts orient this non-clinical area; method and statistics depth depend on the chosen task.

D078:social-research-evaluation.reason: The shared domain foundations already cover question/design, evidence appraisal and communication; add preparation only within the selected task family.

D078:sociology-social-anthropology.reason: Social structures, institutions, culture, inequality, community and social change add subject knowledge beyond generic research-question design.

area_role_overview_reconciliation.role_area_membership_basis: reviewed method/design area-role routes and resolved area-task-family to role-task context edges

role_context_order: carry the selected D078 domain and method or named design into a supported area
show any reviewed area foundation before that area's task-family choices
show the selected area's task-family context and only roles linked to that context
inside each selected role, show role items under their reviewed role task family or an evidence-backed role foundation
keep role tools under the role task they support; never surface role items as a detached pool
role_learning_sequence_contract.item_order_policy: Role progression is ordered by selected area route -> role choice -> reviewed role-task context -> that context's role items and tools. Within one role-task group, only exact reviewed sequence edges order item pairs; all other items are skippable choices in that ordered context. Zero item-pair edges is an explicit source-reviewed disposition, not a missing role route or a stale route-order flag.
role_learning_sequence_contract.role_task_context_policy: A selected area work focus may explain a role task only through a reviewed family-to-role-task edge. Every visible role item must continue through the selected domain -> method/design -> area -> role -> reviewed role task/foundation path. Role-task context is not a qualification, job-readiness finding or universal employer task list.
role_learning_sequence_contract.role_item_placement_policy: Embed a role item under its reviewed role task family. Use a role foundation only when evidence shows it applies across the relevant role tasks. If neither route is supported, keep the item out of student selection; do not create a general standalone role-item lane.
role_learning_sequence_contract.role_prerequisite_note_policy: Preparation notes are preserved under the exact role item as context, not turned into a universal order or blocker. Add a typed prerequisite/workflow edge only with an exact target, route condition and source that supports the relationship.

Computational techniques can be used with qualitative text, surveys and secondary data, so treating this umbrella as the opposite of computational research would mislead learners.

non_pairwise_candidate_dispositions.student_effect: No selectable alternative edge; the source node's statement that simulation does not replace empirical evidence remains as explanatory context.

For sparse categorical-count tables, choose the exact or justified resampling procedure when the large-sample chi-square approximation is unsuitable. The tests have different reference distributions and sampling assumptions.

For independent-binomial 2×2 data, Barnard's unconditional test is an exact alternative when conditioning on both margins is not required. Its an extra unknown value the test has to account for method, variance choice and sampling assumptions differ from Fisher's conditional exact test.

For independent-binomial 2×2 data, Boschloo's unconditional test is an exact alternative based on Fisher's p-value and may be more powerful. State the sampling assumptions and two-sided p-value convention.
For a two-group independent or paired contrast, a rank-based procedure may fit the outcome/design better. It targets a rank/distribution contrast and is not a drop-in mean test.

For independent groups, a rank-based overall alternative may fit when the inferential target is a distribution/location contrast rather than group means. Use a design-matched model when covariates or complex structure matter.

For complete matched blocks with one observation per condition, a rank-based repeated comparison can be an alternative to an appropriate repeated-measures ANOVA. It does not handle every unbalanced or incomplete design.
Probit and logit are alternative link functions for a binomial model of a binary outcome. Compare fit and predicted probabilities/marginal effects rather than raw coefficient scales.

For a prediction/classification goal, tree ensembles can compete with logistic regression as predictive models. Logistic regression remains a distinct inferential GLM and neither model establishes a causal effect.

For the same association question, use Spearman for ordinal/rank or monotonic association where Pearson's linear quantitative association is not the target. Related but distinct coefficients answer different questions.
For the same association question, Kendall is a rank-based alternative when concordance, ordinal measurement or tie handling better fits than Pearson's linear association.
Choose between rank coefficients by the result you set out to estimate, tie pattern, sample and inferential procedure; Kendall tau and Spearman rho are related but not numerically interchangeable.

For high-dimensional or prediction-focused work with collinearity, penalized regression can stabilize or select coefficients relative to OLS. Shrinkage changes estimation and interpretation, so this is a conditional specialist extension rather than a default replacement.

For continuous-outcome prediction, compare nonlinear tree ensembles with a linear baseline on kept-back test data data. The choice is goal- and validation-dependent and neither model is causal by itself.

Count regression provides an outcome-distribution-based inferential model; ML regressors may be compared for prediction but are not direct substitutes for its rate interpretation or inferential the result you set out to estimate.

For prediction/classification tasks, logistic regression can be a transparent statistical baseline beside more flexible supervised models. It is also an inferential generalized linear model. The goals and interpretations differ, so this is not a one-to-one equivalence.

When exploratory evidence suggests a measurement structure, CFA can test a theory-specified structure on suitable independent or kept-back test data evidence. Do not present this as an automatic step or reuse the same data without disclosing it.
Reliability estimates complement a specified measurement model. The coefficient and assumptions must match the scale structure, and reliability is not construct validity.
Reliability estimation complements dimensionality exploration but does not establish that the scale is unidimensional or valid.

IRT and CFA can address measurement structure and comparability through different model frameworks. Choose according to item response format, the result you set out to estimate, sample and assumptions rather than treating scores as equivalent.
ERGMs are a model-based extension for theory-driven inference about tie formation and network dependence. They require network-specific foundations and model diagnostics.
Spatial association analysis builds on defining units and a defensible spatial-weights structure. It describes clustering and dependence, not a causal mechanism.
Spatial lag/error models extend regression to specified spatial dependence and weighting structures. Diagnostics guide model assessment but do not mechanically choose a model.
Moran diagnostics and spatial regression may be used together to examine spatial dependence, but a significant statistic is not an automatic model-selection rule.
The ODD protocol supports transparent ABM specification and reproducibility; it documents a model but does not validate it.
This survey-specific application uses ML response models or ensembles for nonresponse adjustment. Survey design, weighting, variance and bias assessment remain essential.
LLM-based construct measurement is a newer text-as-data technique. Validate construct meaning, scoring stability and subgroup errors against credible references.
CA analyzes sequential interaction and participants’ displayed orientations; CDA examines discourse in relation to social practices and power. They can inform one study but are not interchangeable.
Process tracing structures within-case analysis of causal mechanisms using diagnostic evidence. Its explanatory logic differs from a population-level effect estimate.

Process tracing can examine how a proposed mechanism operates inside cases alongside a design estimating causal effects. Neither substitutes for the other's the result you set out to estimate or assumptions.

Output: a sociological report explaining a social pattern, evidence and limits. typed_relationship_edges.condition: Task/output basis: Understand how public/private decisions allocate activities and infrastructure across places and scales. A research output may compare planned and observed land use/access or explain a spatial trade-off; statutory plans are produced only by appropriately authorized actors. The role evidence is used to test the output context, not to turn an occurrence label into a requirement. Current role-task records: sociologist: Study how people interact and organise into groups, institutions and societies; gather or interpret evidence and explain social patterns. Output: a sociological report explaining a social pattern, evidence and limits. Role-record task evidence excerpt: Sociologists focus their research on explaining social behaviour and the way people have organised themselves as a society. They research and explain the way societies have evolved by describing their legal, political, and economic systems and their cultural expressions.. Authoritative task/profile sources: http://data.europa.eu/esco/occupation/11df8941-508c-4103-ad40-52cdf9430a59 — Exact ESCO occupation profile associated with the current role record; description/scope note and linked knowledge/skills. Output: an economic report with transparent data, model assumptions and qualified conclusions. Role-record task evidence excerpt: Economists perform research and develop theories in the field of economics, whether for microeconomic or macroeconomic analysis. They study trends, analyse statistical data, and to some extent work with economic mathematical models in order to advise companies, governments, and related institutions.. Authoritative task/profile sources: http://data.europa.eu/esco/occupation/99492920-e5a5-4dba-9e5a-93193147198c — Exact ESCO occupation profile associated with the current role record; description/scope note and linked knowledge/skills. Output: a map or place-based report explaining scale, data sources, spatial pattern and limits. Role-record task evidence excerpt: Geographers are scholars who study human and physical geography. Depending on their specialisation, they study political, economical and cultural aspects of humanity contained within human geography. Moreover, they study land formations, soils, natural frontiers, and water flows contained in physica. Authoritative task/profile sources: http://data.europa.eu/esco/occupation/bac64fa2-dcd6-47bb-8e5c-04e04a86a199 — Exact ESCO occupation profile associated with the current role record; description/scope note and linked knowledge/skills. typed_relationship_edges.condition: Task/output basis: Coordinate and integrate methods or concepts from more than one discipline to answer a question that one perspective cannot address adequately. Output is an integrated research design/report that states each contribution, how evidence is combined, and unresolved tensions. The role evidence is used to test the output context, not to turn an occurrence label into a requirement. Current role-task records: behavioural scientist: Formulate evidence-based questions about behaviour in social settings, select suitable observation or measurement methods and interpret behaviour within its context. Output: a research memo distinguishing observed behaviour, measured construct and interpretation. Role-record task evidence excerpt: Behavioural scientists research, observe and describe human behaviour in society. They draw conclusions on the motives that stir actions in humans, observe the various circumstances for different behaviours, and describe different personalities. They advise organisations and governmental institution. area-foundation:d078-economics-economic-.label: Understand economic choices, institutions and outcomes
area-foundation:d078-economics-economic-.meaning: Economics examines how people and institutions make choices, how markets and public systems shape those choices, and how resources and outcomes are distributed. Economic indicators are measurements of parts of that picture; each indicator has a definition and limits.
area-foundation:d078-economics-economic-.description: This starting point adds economic subject knowledge to the research foundations you already met in Social Sciences. It helps you recognize whether a route is about choices, markets, production, distribution, public finance, policy effects or a future estimate. It does not require you to learn every economic measure or analysis method.
area-foundation:d078-economics-economic-.why_it_matters: The same dataset can answer different questions depending on what is measured, who is included and which economic idea is being examined.
area-foundation:d078-economics-economic-.learner_output: A short explanation of the economic idea and outcome a selected analysis is intended to examine, plus one limitation of the measure or evidence.

requirement_scope.condition: Useful across the Economics and Applied Economic Analysis area; review or skip it according to prior knowledge and the selected task.
requirement_scope.rationale: CORE Econ connects distinct economic questions and concepts to different data projects. This is an orientation, not a prerequisite for every economics task.

learning_links.access: Free project-based economics learning resource; each project has its own concepts, data and methods.

area-foundation:d078-sociology-social-an.label: Understand social structures, culture and social change
area-foundation:d078-sociology-social-an.meaning: Sociology and social anthropology study how people live together: how relationships, institutions, culture, inequality and communities shape everyday life, and how people can also change those arrangements.
area-foundation:d078-sociology-social-an.description: This is the subject foundation for Sociology and Social Anthropology. It helps you connect a person's experience to wider relationships, institutions, cultural meanings and social conditions. Your Social Sciences research-question foundation still carries forward; this card adds the area’s subject concepts rather than repeating question-framing advice.
area-foundation:d078-sociology-social-an.why_it_matters: A social pattern is easier to understand when you consider both people's experiences and the wider social setting, rather than treating one example as proof about everyone.
area-foundation:d078-sociology-social-an.learner_output: A brief explanation of a social issue using one relevant concept, the setting or group it concerns, and a limit on what the example can show.

requirement_scope.condition: Useful across Sociology and Social Anthropology; review or skip it according to prior knowledge and the selected task.
requirement_scope.rationale: ASA's sociological literacy framework and Berkeley Anthropology learning goals support these area concepts, but neither makes this a formal entry prerequisite for every route.

area:d078-computational-digital-social-s.label: Computational and Digital Social Science
area:d078-computational-digital-social-s.description: Computational and Digital Social Science uses code, digital traces, networks, text, simulations or other data-intensive approaches to study social processes and digital society. The computational method must remain connected to a social question, sound research design and ethical interpretation; tools such as Python, R or a notebook are ways to carry out work, not the research question itself. Programming is therefore an optional route advantage where the task needs it, not a universal requirement for every Social Sciences learner or role.
